learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of eight data items from a class test is safe to share or a re-identification risk, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** reidentification-risk-checker
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of eight data items from a class test is safe to share or a re-identification risk, with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Anonymized Data, Student Privacy in Testing (defined in this chapter above this block or in Chapter 16). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each item the learner commits one of two bins. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct bin column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the four steps is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) Replacing names with codes makes data anonymous. (2) A group average is always safe. (3) A quotation is harmless if the name is removed. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging whether data can point to a person is an Evaluate-level action. Items that look harmless but identify a student in a class of 24 teach the learner to ask who could pick out a student. **Content:** The two bins: Safe to share, Re-identification risk. The eight items (all made up, for the Watershed Basics pilot of 24 students in one class): | # | Item | Correct bin | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A table with the columns code, version, pre-test, and post-test. | Safe to share | It holds codes and scores only. | | 2 | A table with code, version, pre-test, post-test, class period, teacher name, and gender. | Re-identification risk | In a class of 24 these columns can single out a student. | | 3 | A table with student name, version, pre-test, and post-test. | Re-identification risk | The names identify each student. | | 4 | Comments with names removed and details about seat and appearance removed. | Safe to share | Nothing in them points to one student. | | 5 | A comment that reads "The girl who sits by the window said the video was too fast." | Re-identification risk | The detail points to one student. | | 6 | The average gain for the control group and the average gain for the treatment group. | Safe to share | Each average covers 12 students. | | 7 | The average gain for the 3 students who use captions. | Re-identification risk | A group of 3 is below the size most districts allow to be reported. | | 8 | A file of codes and scores after the key file has been deleted on the stated date. | Safe to share | No link to a person remains. | **Provenance:** The items are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The sim adds the note "your school's rules decide the smallest group you may report". **Rules:** Each item has exactly one correct bin, four per bin. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one item and the two bins. 2. The learner places the item in a bin, and the placement is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After item 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 items in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [bin]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This is [bin]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can tell safe data from risky data." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed item. **Starting State:** The first item in the shuffled order and the two bins. The question shown is "Could someone who knows the class pick out a student?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says that codes alone are not always enough and lists the steps of dropping columns, generalizing, hiding small groups, and cleaning comments.
